title: A hundred and fifteen walks fail on code that passed this afternoon
goal: The scripted walks are the only thing that tells the loop whether the change it just made broke the app. This morning's sweep says 115 of 425 are broken, including every single tutorial. They are not broken: the very same source that passed all 31 tutorial walks yesterday afternoon fails all of them tonight, with nothing changed but the time of day. Find what about the machine or the probe makes a walk answer differently at night, and make a walk answer the same way whoever is or is not sitting at the Mac. Until that is done, every feature the loop ships past the sweep ships on a claim nobody can check, and runners are being sent to hunt bugs that are not there.
notes:
REPRODUCED by the manager pass on 2026-09-15 between 01:45 and 01:55 local. Four walks, one from each failure cluster:

  Scripts/playtest-all.sh appearance-list-min tutorial-mark-it-up size-limits first-run
  ==> 0 passed, 4 failed

  appearance-list-min   step 6 (panelMenu): no menu called "Add Effect" is in the window; the ones that are: ... 25.0pt wide at x 1218.0 says "Add an effect: a shadow, a glow, a border or a blur"
  tutorial-mark-it-up   step 4 (waitFor): mark-it-up step pick-arrow points at tool.arrow, and nothing in the window carries that name (the step was up for 0.5s). The names on screen were: canvas, panel, panel.layers, tool.arrow, ...
  first-run             step 8 (waitFor): take-the-tour step tool-bar points at toolBar, and nothing in the window carries that name. The names on screen were: ... toolBar ...
  size-limits           step 20 (focus): no editable field labelled "Smallest width" is on screen; the ones that are: X, Y, W, H, A, None, None, Padding

Read those errors: two of them say the name is missing and then print the missing name in the list of names that are present. The Add Effect menu IS in the window, at the right size, showing the right tooltip, with an EMPTY name. That shape of contradiction is the whole finding.

THE KEY FACT. The 2026-09-14 16:19 local sweep built at eb474448 and passed 31 of 31 tutorial walks with 5 failures in 396. Check out eb474448 in a throwaway worktree tonight, build it, run the same four walks: all four fail, identically to HEAD. So this is not in the code.

Three hypotheses already tested and DISPROVED, do not repeat them:
  1. The path and outline commit 1ffeff8e, which landed just before the bad sweep. 6e94b8f9 (its parent) fails the same four walks.
  2. c342a75f changing probe-app.sh to 'open -g'. Reverting the -g on HEAD and rerunning: same four failures.
  3. The display being asleep. 'caffeinate -u -t 3' to wake it, then the run under 'caffeinate -d -i': same four failures. Worth knowing anyway that NOTHING in Scripts/ or queue/bin/ calls caffeinate, so no part of the loop asks the machine to stay awake.

What the sweep history says about when it started (counts are from queue/sweep/*.log, tutorials counted with grep '^tutorial-'):
  2026-09-14 01:19 local  385 walks   4 fail   31/31 tutorials pass
  2026-09-14 09:38 local  392 walks   1 fail   31/31 tutorials pass
  2026-09-14 16:19 local  396 walks   5 fail   31/31 tutorials pass   <- last good, built at eb474448
  2026-09-14 17:57 local  330 walks   8 fail   truncated, never reached the tutorials
  2026-09-14 20:42 local   82 walks  19 fail   truncated, and walks that take 5s took 900 to 1045s
  2026-09-15 00:09 local  400 walks 115 fail   31/31 tutorials FAIL

The 20:42 sweep is its own clue: individual walks took a quarter of an hour each. Whatever this is, it makes the app slow as well as unreadable.

LIKELY SAME CAUSE as an-audit-gets-a-real-picture-of-the-app-again, now p1 seq 12: screen capture began failing with SCStreamErrorDomain -3811 the same evening, the last good -sc.png was written at 2026-09-14 20:27, and 'the window has no real presence on screen' would explain a capture that fails, a control with no accessibility name, a tutorial anchor that never resolves and a menu bar that stays frozen all at once. Do these two together.

WHAT IT IS COSTING. queue/tasks/p2-normal/walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep.json logs a runner reproducing turn-into-a-path-walk four separate times on a stashed clean main on the evening of 2026-09-14, inside this window, and concluding it was a real break. Three more walks were written up the same way the same night. Those are runner hours spent on bugs that are probably not in the app.
acceptance: The four walks in the notes pass on an unattended machine, run from a shell with nobody at the keyboard
A sweep run with nobody at the machine reports the same failures as one run while somebody is working at it, proved by running the same subset both ways
Whatever holds the app's window in a state where a walk can read it is done by the harness itself, not by asking a person to leave the screen on
walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep is re-triaged against a trustworthy sweep afterwards, and the walks that were only ever failing for this reason are named in its log
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note:
ROOT CAUSE, with a timestamp. This Mac's screen locked at 2026-09-14 20:46:47 local and has been locked ever since: CGSSessionScreenLockedTime = 1789444007, CGSSessionScreenIsLocked = 1. A locked screen puts the login window over every other window (seen directly: CGWindowList shows loginwindow at layer 2004, 1728x1117, over a probe window at layer 0), so macOS stops drawing the app. Layout and animations stop advancing, the control names SwiftUI reconciles onto AppKit never arrive, and ScreenCaptureKit refuses with -3811.

That is the whole contradiction the task pointed at. Caught live in a diagnostic walk: 'mark-it-up/pick-arrow 1 of 6; tool.arrow at (295, 361) 28x28; card none; host window up, occlusion HIDDEN; NOT FOUND YET after 0.0s on screen'. The anchor IS found, at a rectangle, in that window. TutorialController.place() returned at its occlusion guard before ever recording it, so every tutorial step read 'never found its control' about a tool bar plainly in the window. Same for the Add Effect plus: it is there, right size, right tooltip, and nameless, because .accessibilityLabel is pushed onto the NSPopUpButton during a reconcile that never happens.

It lines up exactly. Last -sc.png any walk wrote: 20:44. Lock: 20:46:47. The 20:42 sweep was four minutes old when it locked, which is why its 5s walks took 900 to 1045s and it reported 19 failures. The 00:09 sweep ran entirely under the lock: 115 of 400, all 31 tutorials.

DISPROVED, so nobody repeats them: not the code (HEAD and eb474448 fail identically), not display sleep (ran under caffeinate -u with UserIsActive 1: same four failures), not alphaValue = 0 on the walk window (set it to 1, rebuilt: same), not a stalled draw (added a 30Hz contentView.display() pump: same), not the Screen Recording grant (CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess still says granted; it is macOS refusing to capture a locked screen).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building.

Walked the idea as somebody who has never seen this. The obvious move is to make walks work while the screen is locked, and it is the wrong one. The only two ways are to draw the app above the login window (app content visible over a locked Mac, a security hole, rejected) or to override somebody's own lock (not ours to do). Even if both worked, a walk would then be judging an app in a state no person ever sees, with animations stalled: the 20:42 sweep is what that looks like, 5s walks taking 900 to 1045s.

Second try: just be more patient. No. Nothing reconciles while nothing is drawn, so the Add Effect plus stays nameless for as long as a walk is willing to wait. Patience is what turned one locked sweep into seventeen hours.

So the shortest thing that delivers the value is not a feature at all: a walk that cannot be trusted says so, and nothing downstream converts that into a bug. An answer you cannot trust is worse than no answer, because it costs whole runner cycles (four are in walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep already) and buries the real breaks in noise. What I deliberately did NOT build: a lock watcher, a wait-for-unlock loop, a notification. The loop already retries between tasks.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, on the built thing.

Ran the whole chain under the real lock rather than reasoning about it, and it found two bugs in my own code. sweep.sh status crashed on an apostrophe inside a single-quoted node -e. And the handback used process.argv.slice(2) where sweep.sh uses slice(1), so the first locked sweep SWALLOWED the pending request instead of handing it back, which is the exact failure the change exists to prevent. Both fixed and re-verified: the request is still pending in queue/sweep/requested.json after a locked run.

Correction to my own earlier reading: I briefly thought tutorial-mark-it-up-walk had passed during a momentary unlock. It had not. I read tail's exit code out of a pipeline. Run without the pipe it is exit 3, status locked, and the -sc.png files I took as proof were stale ones dated Sep 14 17:39. The screen has not unlocked once during this task.

Still clumsy, and I could not fix it: while the screen stays locked the loop retries the pending sweep after every single task, about fifteen seconds each, and the banner says 'running the full walk sweep (about 50 minutes)' before admitting it cannot. And the lock is sampled at the start and the end of a walk, not continuously, so a lock that came and went inside one five second walk would slip through.

VERIFIED, as far as a locked screen allows.

The tutorial half is proved directly, on this locked screen. Same run, same window, occlusion still HIDDEN, and the step now finds its control:

  before  mark-it-up/pick-arrow ... occlusion HIDDEN; NOT FOUND YET after 0.0s on screen
  after   mark-it-up/pick-arrow ... occlusion HIDDEN; found after 0.5s on screen

Run under PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1, the four walks from the task notes now go:
  first-run-walk              13s  ok      (was failing at step 8, waitFor toolBar)
  tutorial-mark-it-up-walk    13s  reaches step 33 (was failing at step 4)
  appearance-list-min          4s  same failure
  size-limits-walk             5s  same failure

The last two are the half no code can fix: the Add Effect plus is nameless and the Smallest width field is absent because the window is never drawn, so SwiftUI never reconciles the label onto the control and never lays the section out. Those two need the screen unlocked, which is what the pending sweep is for.

The refusal path is verified end to end on the real lock:
  Scripts/playtest.sh <walk> --no-build        exit 3, status locked, screenLocked true
  Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build <four>    COULD NOT RUN, exit 3, no walk called failed
  queue/bin/sweep.sh run                       files nothing, request still pending, status says COULD NOT RUN
  Scripts/probe-app.sh                         '==> Grants: ... · screen locked' with the cost underneath
And with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 the same walk runs and reports ok, with screenLocked true still in done.json, so the override buys the run and never the verdict.

Scripts/test.sh: 6667 tests in 537 suites passed.

LEFT ROUGH, none of it earning a task of its own.

Two acceptance items cannot be checked from here. 'The four walks pass on an unattended machine' and 'a sweep with nobody at the machine reports the same failures as one run while somebody is working at it' both need the screen unlocked, and it has been locked since 2026-09-14 20:46:47 with no way for a runner to unlock it. Worth saying that unattended was never the variable: the 01:19 and 09:38 sweeps on 2026-09-14 both ran with nobody at the Mac and passed 31 of 31 tutorials. Locked is the variable. The sweep request is pending and proves both the moment somebody unlocks; walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep carries the re-triage against it.

Third acceptance item is as far as it can go. The harness now holds a run that STARTED unlocked awake for its length, so it cannot be locked out half way, and that is the whole of what a harness can do by itself. It cannot unlock a locked Mac, and the two ways round that are drawing app content over the login window (app content visible on a locked Mac, rejected) or overriding somebody's own lock (not ours). Whether the loop should keep the Mac from locking at all is a real choice about the user's own machine, so it is a decision card rather than something I picked.

Not filed, written here instead: while the screen stays locked the loop retries the pending sweep after every task, about fifteen seconds each, and the banner claims it is 'running the full walk sweep (about 50 minutes)' before admitting it cannot. The lock is sampled at the start and end of a walk rather than continuously, so a lock that came and went inside one five second walk would slip through. And Scripts/playtest/out/ sits untracked in the repo, dirtying git status for every session; it is a walk whose out folder defaults beside the script, and it is being kept deliberately as evidence on an-audit-gets-a-real-picture-of-the-app-again, so I left it.

Nothing to do with Photonz, but the user should know: mobileassetd (pid 610, an Apple daemon) has been holding a core at 93 percent since this Mac booted 167 days ago. Not mine, not something a runner should kill, and not the cause of anything here.

Root cause found and fixed: the Mac's screen locked at 2026-09-14 20:46:47 and has stayed locked, so every walk since read a window macOS was no longer drawing. A walk on a locked screen now reports 'locked' rather than a pass or a failure, playtest-all stops with COULD NOT RUN, the sweep files nothing and keeps its request, and a tutorial step no longer reads 'never found its control' about a control plainly in the window. Shipped in a9b35c96, Scripts/test.sh green (6667 tests). Blocked on a decision only the user can settle: whether the loop should keep the Mac from locking overnight. The two acceptance items that need an unlocked screen are covered by the pending sweep.

EVIDENCE from 2026-09-15 ~15:50, and it points AT the lock detector rather than at the app. Scripts/probe-app.sh printed 'screen locked' and done.json recorded screenLocked: true at both ends of the run, so every walk was being refused. Forced with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1, drag-readout-walk ran 80 steps in 13s, passed, and wrote EIGHT complete 2560x1800 window captures. I opened them: the app is fully drawn — layout done, the right hand panel laid out and readable, a popover mid-dismiss animation, the canvas composited, control names resolving (expect/expectPicked/expectRegion steps all passed against real panel fields). So on this machine right now, the state PlaytestScreenState.isLocked calls 'locked' is one in which the window server IS drawing and IS allowing capture. If that state is the display asleep or the lock screen up over a still-composited session rather than a real lock, the detector is refusing every walk on a machine where walks work perfectly, which is the loop losing its only regression signal for no reason. Worth checking what CGSSessionCopyCurrentDictionary actually reports here before trusting the 115 number: the same reading gates that sweep.

SECOND INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION, 2026-09-15 23:00 local, and it says the same thing as the 15:50 one. I read the flag myself rather than the harness: CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary reports CGSSessionScreenIsLocked = 1, CGSSessionScreenLockedTime = 1789487066 (2026-09-15 08:44 local), kCGSSessionOnConsoleKey = 1, kCGSessionLoginDoneKey = 1 - so by the detector the Mac has been locked for over fourteen hours while the loop worked through task after task. Refused: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/caliper-foot-keeps-its-grip-walk.json -> status locked, 0 of 40 steps, exit 3. Forced: the SAME walk with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 -> status ok, 40 of 40 steps, and one real 2800x2000 window capture (caliper-foot-keeps-its-grip-sc.png). I opened it: the app is completely drawn - the settings screenshot composited on the canvas, the right hand panel laid out with readable labels and its Measurement section, the tool bar, window shadow, and the caliper chip the walk had just dragged reading 103 px. What it is costing: 61 of the 72 sweep logs in queue/sweep say COULD NOT RUN, and the last sweep that actually ran was 2026-09-15 07:31, an hour before this lock began. So the loop's only whole-app regression signal has been dark for fourteen hours on a machine where walks demonstrably run and photograph correctly.
